Again, looking at issues such as duplicity or even implementation, because something— some activity, for example, might have been implemented under a given resolution that is— I mean, that also implements another resolution, so I think we should see them in tandem. But obviously, as the delegate from South Africa mentioned, choosing the clustering is not necessarily objective, or the order in which the clusters will be considered, because Knowing how we operate and who we are, I think there will be long debates on the order of clusters to be examined. But again, I think some sort of clustering is inevitable from a substantive point of view. Thank you very much.

I thank the distinguished representative of Brazil for actually taking the floor again. No one else has pressed the button, and I think that means we have heard the last speaker for today. Thank you so much for your contributions, and I will hand over to my co-chair, Ambassador Wallace, to offer some reflections on what we have heard. So, Brian, you have it.

Thank you so much, Marietta, and thank you, colleagues. I have a script in front of me that I'm respectfully going to depart from, because we've had such a rich discussion today and in the workshops, and it is clear that we have good momentum towards having— maintaining a high-ambition result from this process. There are many areas of convergence, some surprising to us, as co-chairs, including the appetite for a pilot or pilots, but encouraging nevertheless because it demonstrates the will for us to move this process forward in a concrete way. We've heard the cautions. Let me assure you that there is no intent to attempt to derogate from what we have agreed in Resolution 82/51. Those principles are agreed, they're in the resolution, and they will form the basis. So OP25 will exist in relation to everything that we do on review. All of the principles that we have outlined in that resolution will also apply— the balance across the pillars, the effectiveness, efficiency, all of those things. So we already have from 8251 a set of criteria and guidance on modalities that will become the foundation of what we take forward. And then we've heard other things in the room, um, and I don't want to go through and repeat everything because you all heard yourselves talking about the areas of convergence. On the issue of the clusters, I agree that some will take much longer for us to coalesce around, and of course we are still awaiting the Secretary-General's advice in that respect as well. But that having been said, there are some clusters that already some member states have indicated that they would be willing to explore. We heard during the discussions on the resolution, for instance, New Zealand say that they would be be prepared to work with the other co-sponsors, the other core group members of resolutions on the disability architecture, to see whether or not there is scope for consolidation, etc., in relation to that cluster. I have indicated that I am happy to work with my colleagues who have a particular interest in the tourism resolutions to see how we can bring those together. As well around tourism resilience, tourism sustainability, etc. So it is possible for us to approach this not from a directive approach, but in some instances from a voluntary approach. And we encourage all of you to look at those areas of your particular interest that you could consider speaking with your colleagues about to see whether there is scope. I think that collaborative spirit would help us to generate consensus because the interested, the most interested parties would have initiated that sort of clustering. And we know what our individual priorities are, and without that being imposed on everyone, I think that would be also a good, potentially a good place to start. The timelines are set out in the resolution to guide our work, and we are mandated to develop the criteria and modalities by the end of August. Whether or not those will remain— what we develop by then will remain fixed is a matter for us. And if we decide that we will set out a framework for the modalities and the criteria and have them tested in pilot projects, reporting back to this Working Group, and wrapped up at the end of the life of this Working Group in April of next year, then that would be, to my mind, a perfectly appropriate way to go. Because at the end of the day, what we want to do is to achieve a useful meaningful, long-term result, rather than ticking the box that we've completed something on a checklist by a certain time. So I think from this discussion today, we have received very clear guidance from you in concretizing the proposals on criteria and modalities, and we will work with the Secretary on fleshing out exactly what formats are possible. The idea that we should revert to the decision-making body for mandates, I think, is very much common sense and will give us an opportunity to filter the broad scope of mandates that we have into manageable chunks. But I think it was the delegation of South Africa, the distinguished DPR, who pointed out the need for us to be coherent as member states across the committees. And I know that many of you who are in this Working Group do not sit in every other committee. There are some of us from very small delegations who double up and triple up, but many of you have your work in, in this Working Group, and another colleague will be in one in Second Committee and another in Third Committee. And we know that they have their own cultures and hold on to those individual cultures very dearly. It is important for us in our own capacities as member states to make sure that we carry the message to our colleagues so that when we establish a mechanism as between us as co-chairs and the PGA and the chairs of the committees, to bring to the attention of the committees that we expect and hope to inspire implementation of this resolution in their work, that it is well received already because you have helped us to lay the foundations for that to be well received there. So we're counting on you to do that. Have the conversations. I cannot emphasize this enough. Have the conversations with your respective committee colleagues. With your ECOSOC colleagues. And then we will see how we can filter through the implementation reviews there that will lead to good decisions about whether mandates need to remain and whether there is scope for us to have to review whether they should continue. There was also a suggestion that in the committees, the Secretariat could provide us with a snapshot of where implementation is in respect of those mandates, to give us a sense at the very start of consideration when they come up in the committees of what that particular mandate looks like. I'm very pleased to report that your diligent co-chairs, along with a very diligent Secretariat, is already working on, on that, because we recognize the central role of the Secretariat to provide the information to support member states' decision-making. And so we expect that to be ready for rollout in the 81st session during the committees. So you will have that— I hope you will have that sort of new aspect of Secretariat introduction of mandates there to flesh out your deliberations. So, I'm going to hand the floor back to my co-chair to just talk a little bit about the next steps in a minute. But there are a couple of things that we do have to think about a little bit as co-chairs, and we are going to be consulting with you on this, on how would the pilot review, what would be the format for that? Is that something that we assign, and how would we derive that power to assign responsibility for that pilot? So there are some sort of framing questions that we have to answer on that, and we're happy to receive your suggestions and guidance on how that could work. As I said, on timing, we will meet the deadlines that we have. We ask that the deadlines that we meet are construed flexibly enough so that we have the possibility of making common sense adjustments and are not tied to, for instance, the 31st of August modalities. If we discover that in pilots they need tweaking, and we can't then say, oh, but we agreed this on the 31st of August and therefore we can't change it before the end of April. Again, maintaining that sort of common sense, pragmatic approach to how we go about our work. So, very encouraged by the discussions today. I think we will be able to come back to you in fairly short order. We have to come back to you on the Secretary-General's reports soon. We will come back to you as well on the technical briefing, but Marietta, if you want to just take us through the next steps.

Thank you so much, Brian, and it's so important that we remain practical in this work because this is really about making us function better together. I just wanted to talk just a little bit of— about next steps. I mean, there's There's a lot of reflection to be done by us, as Brian said, but you will recall that we completed the first stage of this work regarding the templates with a sort of mutual shared understanding about how the membership will proceed with them, using them, absent a formal decisions. Um, on decision-making for this stage of our work, we, we have to consider how to finalize this aspect of work, and we will need to consider together whether we will need to take a formal decision in this working group or whether we will need to forward something to the General Assembly based on a report from this working group, and we are very, very open to your suggestions regarding this, but please think about it. And as you may have noticed as well, this is the last meeting outlined in our roadmaps that we circulated to you in May. As has been said, we will now continue to reflect on what we have heard from you. We will refine ideas and views that have been expressed so far on criteria and on modalities, also with the help of the Secretariat. But so this is the last scheduled meeting for now, but we do remain as always ready to continue these conversations outside the formal room and together with you in your spaces and places, should you so wish. But please do not hesitate to react to us or to our teams at any stage. Send any thoughts, ideas, or statements that you have ready. So send that through our regular email address, which is unatmandates.co-chairs@gmail.com. Um, and as previously also announced, we aim to wrap up this work before the summer break, so you will hear from us shortly. And with that, we close the meeting.
